author: scouts970
quote:
GTA VI is a 13-year con job that finally arrived and proved every cynical prediction true. Locked at a greasy 30 frames per second on every console including the Pro, the whole thing stutters the second more than three cars share the same street. Characters fall through the map, clip through furniture, swim sideways, and softlock missions before the prologue even ends. For eighty dollars and a 200+ gigabyte install that comes as a code in a box, this is the reward. 

The sandbox is gone. Rockstar traded pure GTA chaos for a slow, preachy relationship simulator where Lucia and Jason constantly nag each other and the game punishes you for having fun. Kill too many pedestrians and the morality system brands you “irredeemable,” nerfs your abilities, and forces the story down a duller path. No prostitutes. No cheating. No wild anonymous mayhem without consequences. Just long drives, mini-golf, dog-walking, and cutscenes about feelings. The map looks pretty from a distance and feels empty the moment you try to actually live in it.

Jason and Lucia have all the personality of wet cardboard. The writing is the worst in the series, forced, self-serious, and terrified of offending anyone. Missions are padded with chores and hand-holding. The freedom that defined every previous game has been replaced by a carefully managed narrative experience that wants you to care about these two mid protagonists and their domestic drama. It plays more like a lesser Red Dead Redemption 2 with palm trees than anything that deserves the Grand Theft Auto name.

Bugs, performance, pacing, characters, story, missing features, political sanitizing, and pure overhype. Thirteen years of waiting produced a beautiful-looking, tightly controlled, joyless slog that reviews called a masterpiece while the actual players who paid for it got the truth. This is not GTA. This is the biggest disappointment in gaming history.
